new_entities.name: Wearable oximetry for obstructive sleep apnea screening
new_entities.description: Consumer or medical wearable oximetry approaches used to screen for obstructive sleep apnea before confirmatory testing.

new_entities.name: Diagnosis
new_entities.description: Identification of the presence or absence of a target condition.

edges.effect_quant: Wearable oximetry can screen for OSA fairly well, but it should complement rather than replace formal testing. A 2025 meta-analysis found wearable sensitivity 0.87, specificity 0.86, and AUC 0.93 for AHI greater than 15, while older single-device studies showed respectable but variable performance across thresholds and populations.
edges.population: adults being screened for suspected obstructive sleep apnea, especially where access to standard testing is limited
edges.mechanism: Nocturnal desaturation patterns, oxygen desaturation indices, and photoplethysmographic signatures can reflect recurrent obstructive breathing events and help triage patients toward definitive testing.
edges.summary: There is real signal here, especially for moderate to severe OSA screening, but the edge is mixed because performance depends heavily on device type, threshold, and clinical context.
edges.caveats: Wearable oximetry is better for screening than for ruling out all OSA. It can miss milder disease, arousal-heavy disease, and some patients without pronounced desaturation, and false positives can arise from other causes of nocturnal hypoxemia.

evidence.notes: Diagnostic value of wearable and contactless technologies for detecting obstructive sleep apnea: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: Pooled wearable-device sensitivity for detecting OSA at AHI greater than 15
